title: Patch a punctured bicycle inner tube
instruction: Apply the orange patch over the marked puncture, press it down firmly and leave it sealed after releasing both hands.
context: A small emergency bicycle repair: positioning a flexible adhesive patch is only useful if its bond seals the puncture. The operator has already cleaned and lightly abraded the rubber and removed the backing.
setup: A standard butyl 20-inch inner tube (Decathlon 8640844, 38/47-406, no sealant) lies in the photographed 420 x 320 mm oval with a single upward-facing puncture made by a 1.2 mm pin. The clean, dry, abraded target is marked outside the bonding area. One fresh Park Tool GP-2 pre-glued patch is unbacked on a 35 x 35 mm silicone release card, 70 mm nearer and 115 mm to the robot’s right of the hole. The simulator approximates the patch as a 24 x 24 x 0.4 mm orange sheet. README.md gives preparation, physical-size checks and reset.
scoring: 1.0: intact patch seals the puncture and remains sealed with both hands released for 3 seconds. 0.75 for a sealed patch still held or before the hold ends. 0.25 for a partly bonded patch covering the puncture but still leaking. Otherwise 0. Damage overrides all credit. Physical check after release: install in the specified 20-inch tyre, inflate to 40 psi, and lose at most 2 psi over 5 minutes after a 60-second settling period, without adding air. README.md defines the pump/gauge check and partial-credit inspection. Do not inflate a GP-2 repair outside a tyre.
fidelity: Native YAM arms/cameras. Patch is a flexible mass-point sheet; pressure and dwell create local adhesive bonds that can peel. A connected unbonded path from puncture to patch edge predicts leakage on a 3 mm grid. This is an uncalibrated seal proxy, not air/glue chemistry. Tube is a supported reduced curved surface with lateral motion, not a full pressure/deformation model. Grips are idealized.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0; scripted demo: 1.0. Dream completed with 21 server sessions after expiry recoveries.
reset_notes: Use a fresh GP-2 patch and a fresh, same-model tube with one prepared puncture per trial. Make the hole, clean, abrade and dry the target by the numbered README protocol. No glue, sealant or reused adhesive. Keep exposed adhesive and judging liquids away from the gripper pads. Physical leak judging is performed after the trial in a matching tyre, not by stretching the patched tube outside it.
